item.title: Notre Dame Hockey: Irish take No. 4 Michigan State down in the shootout
item.description: Notre Dame playing really good hockey right now, and after sweeping Penn State, the Irish just went 1-0-1 against Michigan State — the No. 4 team in the country. Notre Dame won the shootout on Friday night to give them the extra points. Irish Outlast #4 Spartans In Shootout SOUTH BEND, Ind. – The Notre Dame Fighting Irish battled No. 4 Michigan State to a 1-1 stalemate on Friday evening inside Compton Family Ice Arena before claiming the second point with a shootout victory to grab four points against the top-5 ranked opponent over the two games. The Irish are now unbeaten over their last four games and move to 5-6-1 on the season and 3-2-1 in Big Ten play. Freshman goaltender Patrick Quinlan continues his run of great play in between the pipes, as he was named the First Star of the Game. Quinlan made 34 saves while allowing just one into the back of his net before not allowing a single Michigan State player to score in the shootout. Evan Werner scored Notre Dame’s goal in regulation and now has a team-high six goals on the season. An unsung hero of the game was Pano Fimis, who continued his incredible form at the dot, winning 15-of-22 faceoffs. HOW IT HAPPENED For the second-straight night the Irish and Spartans played a scoreless first period, as the two sides went into the first intermission deadlocked at 0-0. Quinlan made some key stops early in goal before the Irish attack started to really pressure the Michigan State net. Shots were nearly even at the end of the opening 20 minutes of play as the Spartans held a narrow lead at 9-8. The back-and-forth contest continued throughout the second period, with neither team giving an inch. Notre Dame managed to kill a penalty at the start of the second and one at the end to keep the game scoreless through 40 minutes of play. Notre Dame’s offense generated a number of quality chances in the second period but were unable to find the back of the net. The Irish earned a power play in the opening minutes of the third period and Evan Werner nearly put Notre Dame in front but his effort was turned away by the Michigan State goaltender. As regulation began to wind down, both teams pushed for the winner and it appeared that the Irish found it at the 17:41 mark of the third, as Werner made an unbelievable individual effort to get to the front of the crease before using a perfect backhand finish to give Notre Dame the 1-0 lead. Unfortunately, the Spartans answered less than a minute later, as Tommi Mannisto scored to level the score at 1-1 and send the game into overtime for the second-straight evening. Notre Dame was the more likely team to score in the extra session, as it outshot the visitors 4-2 in the 5-minute overtime but were unable to produce the winner as the game officially ended in a tie. The shootout ensued to determine which team would earn the extra point. item.title: Stats: Real Madrid summer signing delivers sensational performance with two assists in 7-0 international victory
item.description: Stats: Real Madrid summer signing delivers sensational performance with two assists in 7-0 international victory Real Madrid have enjoyed an impressive run of form under Jose Mourinho, with competition for places across the pitch intensifying. At right-back in particular, the manager has to choose between three high-quality options. Denzel Dumfries started the season as Mourinho’s first-choice right-back but has slipped down the pecking order , with Federico Valverde taking over the role. However, the Dutchman has not let his club situation affect his international form, putting in a brilliant display against Greece. Dumfries involved in three goals against Greece He reminded everyone of his outstanding attacking ability, playing a part in three goals in the Netherlands’ 6-0 victory. The Madrid defender played the full 90 minutes and registered two assists, while also playing an important role in a third goal. His first contribution came in the 33rd minute, when he provided a headed assist for Tijjani Reijnders to complete his hat-trick. Dumfries was involved again in the 59th minute, delivering a dangerous cross that was parried by the Greek goalkeeper, allowing Jurrien Timber to convert the rebound. Just three minutes later, the 30-year-old produced an excellent individual move before setting up Donyell Malen for the Netherlands’ seventh goal. Interestingly, Dumfries registered just 43 touches throughout the encounter but made excellent use of them. He completed 24 of his 26 passes with 92% accuracy. He also created three chances, including one big opportunity, and registered seven touches in the opposition penalty area. An attacking display that will encourage Mourinho The most interesting aspect of Dumfries’ performance was his constant presence in dangerous attacking positions. The defender accumulated 0.77 expected goals despite failing to score. This has always been a feature of his game. Dumfries has had a mixed start to life at Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Even at Real Madrid, Dumfries often occupied positions inside the opposition penalty area, but that left the team exposed defensively. For Mourinho, Dumfries offers a very different dimension. His crossing ability could add a potent weapon to Los Blancos ‘ attack. With Federico Valverde and Trent Alexander-Arnold also competing for opportunities at right-back, it remains to be seen how Mourinho manages Dumfries’ playing time in the coming games. Stats: FotMob

item.title: ‘Really proud’ – Aaron Rodgers shares rare photo with ‘little bro’ Jordan in relationship update
item.description: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers’ family circumstances have been a big talking point throughout his career, but the veteran quarterback has been working on fixing those relationships of late. The 42-year-old is playing into the final months of his career in the NFL, as he prepares to hang up his cleats at the end of the current season. The Pittsburgh Steelers are in a good position, but this weekend’s game against the Cincinnati Bengals will tell a lot about where they are. Along the journey of his final season in the league, Rodgers is clearly looking for opportunities to bring his family along on the journey. Taking to his Instagram account, the Steelers’ quarterback has now shared a photo of himself and his younger brother, Jordan, in a rare sighting of the two together. Aaron Rodgers admits he’s ‘proud’ of younger brother Jordan in rare sighting together Rodgers’ younger brother Jordan works for ESPN, and has been working as part of their coverage for this weekend’s upcoming College Football fixtures. On Friday evening, the Acrisure Stadium hosted Pittsburgh vs Florida State. With Jordan working for ESPN’s coverage at the home of the Steelers, it provided Aaron with the perfect opportunity to catch up with his younger brother. Taking to Instagram, Rodgers said: “Great to see little bro @jrodgers11 in his element tonight @acrisurestadium. Really proud of how hard he’s worked to get to where he is now 👊🏻.” The photo shared showed the pair smiling from ear to ear, with fans in the comments sharing their delight at seeing the two brothers together. Their relationship has been strained over the years, with Jordan admitting as much on television shows in the past. However, this marks a real step forward in patching up their relationship, with Rodgers seemingly looking for a settled life as he prepares to call it a day on his career. Jordan Rodgers praised Aaron recently on ESPN for his skills at quarterback, but he will certainly cherish his improved relationship with his brother over what he is able to do on a football field. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty The Georgia football head coach Kirby Smart has never been one to hide his affection for the SEC, and for good reason. His program has experienced what winning the conference means. But with the SEC championship game approaching its final edition, Smart is making clear that accepting the decision does not mean liking it. Speaking with Paul Finebaum in an interview shared by SEC Network, Smart defended the event’s place in college football. He described it as one of the country’s greatest sporting events. He also offered a comparison that should get the attention of fans outside the conference. “I’m not excited about not having an SEC championship game,” Smart said. “It’s something I don’t control, and I’ve accepted it.” Kirby Smart Defends SEC Championship Game The SEC announced Nov. 9 that its 2026 championship game would be the last. The conference’s announcement described the end of a run that began in 1992. For fans accustomed to building their December around that matchup, the change removes a part of the season. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Smart’s comments suggest he sees more being lost than a game on the schedule. A conference championship brings together teams that have spent months trying to earn that opportunity. Winning it provides its own accomplishment, even when a national championship remains the goal. “I think it’s one of the greatest sporting events in the country,” Smart said. “Next to the national championship game, it’s the biggest game in the year.” That is a strong endorsement from someone whose job involves preparing for those stakes. Smart is not separating the SEC title from the national conversation. He is arguing that the event deserves a prominent place within it. item.title: Grady Hirst-led West Branch football upsets Rocky River in OHSAA playoffs
item.description: ROCKY RIVER — Grady Hirst ran for two touchdowns in the final 5:37 as West Branch (11-1) rallied for an impressive 21-12 win over previously unbeaten Rocky River (11-1) in a Division IV, Region 13 semifinal on the road. Hirst gave West Branch the lead with a 2-yard touchdown with 5:37 to play and then sealed the win with another 2-yard TD run with just 3:27 left. Hirst ran for 203 yards and all three West Branch touchdowns on 36 carries. The Youngstown State recruit was 11-of-18 passing for 84 yards with no interceptions. Gavin Marshall put an exclamation point on the victory with an interception on Rocky River's final drive that allowed West Branch to take a knee to run out the clock and advance. Jeremy Ramsey also intercepted a pass for West Branch. Marshall led West Branch in receiving with five catches for 54 yards. Watch Ohio High School Football Live on NFHS Network all year Rocky River scored two first-quarter touchdowns but was shut out the rest of the game. Carter Atwater threw a touchdown and ran for a touchdown for the Pirates. Rocky River missed an extra point after its first touchdown and failed to convert a 2-point conversion pass on its second touchdown. That allowed West Branch to take a 14-12 lead with 5:32 remaining in the fourth quarter after Hirst scored on a 2-yard run. Rocky River was limited to just seven first downs and 173 yards of total offense. Kentucky recruit Tristin Hughes was held to 44 yards receiving on three catches for Rocky River. Rocco Baon was the top offensive performer for the Pirates with 50 yards rushing on 16 carries. West Branch got two pass deflections on defense from Landon Coffee. Coffee also caught a key 2-point conversion from Hirst with 3:27 left to extend the West Branch lead to nine points and make it a two-possession game. West Branch advances to the Division IV, Region 13 championship game against No. 5-seeded West Geauga (11-2) on Friday, Nov. 20. The game will be played at a site to be determined. item.title: Villarreal forward opens door to Barcelona move with admission about childhood dream: ‘Club of my heart’
item.description: Villarreal forward opens door to Barcelona move with admission about childhood dream: ‘Club of my heart’ Villarreal striker Georges Mikautadze has admitted that Barcelona have been the club of his heart since childhood, describing the Catalan side’s interest in him as flattering while expressing his ambition to earn a move to one of Europe’s biggest clubs. In an interview with DAZN , the Georgia international discussed Barcelona’s previous interest and made it clear that the speculation has provided additional motivation. His comments are particularly interesting given that Barcelona considered him as a potential attacking reinforcement during the summer of 2026, when the club was assessing options for the future of Robert Lewandowski. Mikautadze admits Barcelona have been his dream club Discussing the links with Barcelona, Mikautadze admitted that he is a lifelong Barcelona fan and it makes him happy that they were interested in him. Georges Mikautadze admits he is a Barcelona fan. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) “Barcelona has been the club of my heart since I was a kid. It’s flattering to hear about their interest. “I still watch the Barcelona games… But it’s up to me to work hard and earn the chance to move to a big club like Barcelona,” he revealed. It is crucial to remember that the Georgian forward has previously explained that his admiration developed during the era of Xavi, Andres Iniesta, Sergio Busquets and the famous attacking partnership known as MSN. “Barcelona’s interest? Yes, it’s flattering and gives me even more motivation. It also means I’m doing a good job. Georges Mikautadze is ready to take the next big step in his career. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) “Besides, when I was young, I was a Barcelona fan, ever since the days of Xavi, Iniesta, Busquets and MSN. But I hadn’t really thought much about it,” he had said. Barcelona faced financial obstacles despite Mikautadze’s interest Meanwhile, Mikautadze also talked about his readiness to take the next step in his career, despite recognising that he still has room to improve. “I’ve turned 26, but I think I’m ready to move to a big club. I have everything it takes, and I try to show that every time. Maybe I just need a little more time,” he said. However, it must be remembered that Villarreal are in a strong negotiating position, as his release clause increased from €60 million to €78 million in August 2026, while his contract also runs until 2031.

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino: why the newly appointed Man United manager will take this star to the stratosphere
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino: why the newly appointed Man United manager will take this star to the stratosphere Manchester United have not made the best signings in recent years. Last summer was seen as an outlier, though, as all four players, Matheus Cunha , Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Senne Lammens, all played key roles as United went from 15th to third in the league. This season has evidently been a disaster so far, as they sit 18th in the league in November, and Michael Carrick has paid for this start with his job. Matheus Cunha Whilst Cunha has not hit the heights of last season, he has still provided four goals and five assists in all competitions. This included a stunning brace to beat AS Roma in a magical night at Old Trafford in the Champions League earlier this month. Nonetheless, Cunha struggled under Carrick at times, playing as a number nine and being shunted out of his natural position to accommodate Marcus Rashford since his return this season. Mauricio Pochettino will love him Much has been made of incoming Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino’s admiration for Rashford , but he will arguably love Cunha’s profile more. Cunha will fit the Argentine’s tactics like a glove. According to Premier League analysis , Pochettino favours “a 4-2-3-1 system where wide attackers operate as roaming inside forwards rather than rigid touchline wingers. Starting on the left, Cunha can drift centrally into the pockets between midfield and defence while an overlapping full-back.” The Brazil international always looks more dangerous when he has licence to drift in and out and also drop into midfield, so this will be great news for him. In addition, players like Dele Alli and Cole Palmer, who like to operate in the half-spaces, have traditionally done well for Pochettino, so there is no reason to believe Cunha cannot also benefit. The former Tottenham Hotspur coach’s system also heavily relies on high pressing, and United are not a team full of natural pressers. Cunha, however, is great at pressing and harrying defenders into mistakes, and it seems natural that he would adapt well to Pochettino’s demands. What’s more, the head coach also likes to employ fast transitions in attack and, once again, Cunha has often hurt teams in England like this for Wolverhampton Wanderers and United. Finally, the head coach is renowned for his ability to man-manage and forge strong relationships with players. Therefore, he may just be the man to get the occasionally erratic Cunha to click, feel loved and stay on task. Featured image by Justin Setterfield via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Barcelona, Real Madrid, PSG, Milan and Brighton tracking young Brazilian star
item.description: BELO HORIZONTE, BRAZIL - SEPTEMBER 12: Vitao (C) of Atletico Mineiro celebrates with teammates after scoring the team's third goal during the Brasileirao 2026 27th-round match between Atletico Mineiro and Fluminense at Arena MRV on September 12, 2026 in Belo Horizonte, Brazil. (Photo by Pedro Vilela/Getty Images) | Getty Images The two La Liga giants, two other big teams in Europe, and one team from England are among the European clubs after Vitor Fernandes Chaves Teixeira, also known simply as Vitão, according to a new report . An U17 FIFA World Cup champion with Brazil, Vitão has broken through at Atlético Mineiro in his national league, and many clubs in Europe have taken note. A tall center-back who recently scored his first senior level goal, Vitão is said to be tracked by FC Barcelona, Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain, AC Milan, and Brighton. The Galo is said to be willing to let him go for £12 million, which would be a significant sale for them. He has a contract until 2028. The Brazilian league is due to end in December, so there is a chance that he goes in the European winter transfer window, though the report notes the club wants to keep him until summer 2027 if possible. Barcelona is on the hunt for new defenders, being somewhat thin in the center-back position due to a combination of injuries, loss of form, and the departure of Iñigo Martínez in the transfer window last year. Still just 18 years old, Vitão may not be fully ready to contribute at elite teams in Europe just yet. But there is a growing feeling that he will be making the jump across the Atlantic to the top five leagues sooner rather than later.

Hodgson reflected on just how much the Bayern Munich striker has evo “Harry Kane, of course. We had Harry Kane for a short period of time. We took him in just before the Euros, but that was 10 years ago. item.description: As Scotland legend Kenny Dalglish watched one of his records equalled in Scotland's 2-1 win over North Macedonia, another of his feats loomed into view. The night was supposed to be about Andy Robertson joining Dalglish as Scotland's most-capped man, the Tottenham left-back making his 102nd appearance for his country. But instead, for the first time, the 75-year-old might be nervous that his crown as one of Scotland men's all-time top goalscorers is wobbling. That is because, in Scotland's rather humdrum Nations League victory, John McGinn - in his 94th Scotland appearance - took two big strides towards the record. The Aston Villa midfielder now has 24 goals for his country - six shy of Dalglish's long-standing record of 30, shared with Denis Law. "It's something that's been in the back of my head," McGinn admitted in the post-match debrief. "If I start climbing that table, it means we've been successful as a team." Now 32 years old, time is running out for him. But as he pulls level with Hughie Gallacher, one of the Wembley Wizards of folklore, his ambition is clear. McGinn double gives drab Scotland win over North Macedonia The rise and rise of 'Meatball' McGinn McGinn 'definitely capable' of reaching record There was a time when talk of this record being toppled seemed laughable. Scotland has produced strikers in recent decades, but none close to Dalglish or Law. The fact a midfielder might take the title makes McGinn's feat all the more astonishing. His prowess in front of goal is no secret to the Tartan Army. There was the spell at the end of 2019 where he scored six in three games, his overhead kick against Austria, his late winner against Croatia in 2024. But of late, his lack of goals and even his performances have had some fans questioning where he fits into the Scotland team. "It has been a bit of a dry patch for me over the last year on the goal front," McGinn admitted, and he's not wrong. He failed to find the back of the net for Scotland in 2025, the first time he'd done that since 2020. But, just as his form at Villa has sky-rocketed, he came up big for his new international head coach Sebastien Pocognoli. "Isn't it great to have a John McGinn in your team?" former Scotland winger Pat Nevin said on Sportsound. "He's somebody you'd want to have in your team to be taking a penalty for you. item.title: David Warner accuses Cricket Australia of ‘cover up’ over sandpaper scandal
item.description: David Warner has sensationally accused Cricket Australia (CA) of executing a “cover-up” of the “sandpapergate” ball-tampering scandal in 2018. Warner, then vice-captain, was one of three players to serve long bans after a CA investigation into the use of sandpaper on the ball during the Test series against South Africa. Usman Khawaja had reopened the saga by writing in his autobiography that the whole Australian team were aware of the ball tampering, drawing support from close friend Warner and a strong denia l from now-skipper Pat Cummins . Warner, who retired from international cricket in January 2024, has now claimed that Cummins and the rest of the bowling attack – who have always denied wrongdoing – were not interviewed as part of the investigation. David Warner (left), Cameron Bancroft and Steve Smith all served bans for their role in the ball tampering scandal (Reuters) “As far as l am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood , Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation," Warner said in a post on Instagram. "If that's correct, then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn't know? "It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning, ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea. That stinks of a cover-up." Cummins suggested on Friday that he had been talked to as part of enquiries in 2018. He, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon have always maintained that they were unaware that sandpaper was brought on to the field in Cape Town to tamper with the ball. Australia captain Pat Cummins spoke to the media for more than an hour as he responded to Usman Khawaja’s claims (Reuters) Warner, captain Steve Smith and batter Cameron Bancfroft were the only players punished by Cricket Australia in 2018. Head coach Darren Lehmann was cleared of wrongdoing, though resigned his role at the end of that series. In response to the former opener’s new claim, a Cricket Australia statement said: “As we have stated previously, all players were given the opportunity to speak at the time of the initial investigation and have had the ability to come forward with new evidence in the eight years since. "Subsequently, CA has respected every player and former players' right to provide their own version of events." CA has previously said that it does not intend to reopen the investigation.

item.description: FBL-WC-2026-MATCH88-AUS-EGY - AFP Mohamed Salah has officially written his name into the history books as Egypt's all-time leading goalscorer. The 34-year-old forward netted twice late on in a dominant 5-0 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying victory over Malawi, sealing the milestone with a piece of outrageous audacity. Salah makes history in dominant Pharaohs win Salah has officially become Egypt's all-time leading goalscorer after netting a late brace against Malawi. The 34-year-old forward struck twice in the closing stages to inspire his nation to a commanding 5-0 victory . Salah entered the international break sitting just two goals shy of the long-standing national benchmark. By the time the final whistle blew, the veteran attacker had claimed the prestigious honour outright in front of an ecstatic crowd. Audacious Panenka seals landmark 70th strike The Trabzonspor star left it late to rewrite the record books during a frantic finale. Salah finally drew level with previous record-holder Hossam Hassan in the 84th minute, finding the back of the net to reach 69 international goals. Rather than settling for a share of the crown, the forward snatched the outright record in stoppage time. Awarded a penalty in added time, Salah showed remarkable composure to beat the goalkeeper with an audacious Panenka, securing his landmark 70th goal in style. Relentless form continues following Anfield departure Salah's latest milestone extends an international career that began back in 2011. Across 123 appearances for the Pharaohs, he has consistently delivered on the biggest stages while cementing his legacy as an icon of African football. His prolific touch remains intact at club level following his move to Turkey. Another major chapter in a legendary career Breaking Egypt's national scoring record adds to an extraordinary list of individual honours. Prior to his switch to Trabzonspor, Salah spent nine memorable years at Liverpool , departing Anfield as the club's all-time top scorer in the Premier League with 191 goals. item.title: Detroit Red Wings: Stopping The Skid
item.description: SUNRISE, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 12: Anton Lundell #15 of the Florida Panthers scores the game-winning goal against John Gibson #36 of the Detroit Red Wings at Amerant Bank Arena on November 12, 2026 in Sunrise, Florida. The Panthers defeated the Red Wings 5-4. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images) Getty The Detroit Red Wings have now lost five games straight, including two at home, before embarking on a four-game road trip. It’s no longer about making the playoffs, but salvaging a season that has been fraught with chaos and controversy. Last night’s loss to the Florida Panthers marked the second time in which the Red Wings blew a multi-goal lead in less than two weeks. Head Coach Todd McLellan had the following to say in his post-game comments: “I don’t think we lost our poise. We lost our momentum that we worked really hard to earn in the first 40 minutes of the game. A team like that, that’s won cups recently and has that type of cache, they take advantage of that, and we’re still learning how to deal with it.” As has been the case with a majority of matchups so far this season, coming close doesn’t cut it; the team needs to find ways to finish. Plugging The Positional Holes It’s no secret that the Detroit Red Wings are hurting for depth at Center. While Marco Kasper has shown promising two-way play since his return from injury on Tuesday and Emmitt Finnie seems to be handling his new role with confidence, a true 1C has yet to emerge in Dylan Larkin’s absence. It’s widely thought that the Wings will need to look outside of their current roster for this, though the 10 teams on Larkin’s trade list aren’t necessarily willing to give one up at this point. Simon Edvinsson’s absence can also be heavily felt. Second in average ice time per game, only to Moritz Seider, the left-shot defenseman and his partner were one of the top pairings in the league before the Red Wings’ centennial season took a nosedive earlier this year. With the December 1st deadline quickly approaching and Edvinsson adamant about being traded, they may very well have played their last game together. item.title: ‘Stephon Castle Gave Yaxel Lendeborg His Welcome to the NBA Moment’ — NBA Fans Roast Warriors Rookie After ‘Alpha’ Talk Backfires vs. Spurs
item.description: Collage featuring BASKETBALL-NBA-SAS-DAL/ and BASKETBALL-NBA-SAS-DAL/. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The San Antonio Spurs opened the game with an 18-0 run Friday night and never let the Golden State Warriors back into it, rolling to a 123-85 win at Frost Bank Center. Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg recorded a season-low 3 points while the Spurs’ Stephon Castle poured in a game-high 32, and fans did not hold back in their assessment. The rough outing came only hours after a clip emerged of Lendeborg discussing taking on a bigger role with Stephen Curry sidelined. Warriors’ Yaxel Lendeborg Goes Cold Hours After Discussing Bigger Role Lendeborg, the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, entered the night averaging 21.7 points on 51.8% shooting. Against San Antonio, he shot 1-of-13 from the field, missed both of his 3-point attempts, and committed 3 turnovers. His minus-40 in 24 minutes was the worst mark of anyone on the floor. At Friday morning’s shootaround, Lendeborg discussed how he planned to approach Curry’s absence. “In general, I do got to start thinking more like an alpha dog rather than beta, or whatever’s after beta. I’m definitely gonna try to shift the mindset.” Once the night got away from Golden State, one fan summed it up by pointing to San Antonio’s top scorer: “Stephon Castle gave Yaxel Lendeborg his welcome to the NBA moment.” A Los Angeles Lakers fan account mocked the Warriors rookie and pointed to the shooting line: “Yaxel Lendeborg 1/13 FG.” Lendeborg’s only field goal was a 9-foot floater with 4:13 left in the second quarter, when the Warriors were already down 27. Another fan zeroed in on the final count. “He went 1-for-13 from the field.” Yet another fan went further and highlighted the defense he faced and remarked , “Yaxel Lendeborg fake demon when he go up against real defense … 1 for 13. Spurs got that boy in prison.” For another hoops observer, the answer was to look ahead. “This Yaxel Lendeborg performance never happened. We move.” Castle’s night went right the other way. He scored his 32 points on 12-of-18 shooting, hit 5-of-8 from 3-point range, and added 6 assists while finishing plus-35, doing all of it in 25 minutes. Early in the third quarter, Castle blocked a Lendeborg layup. Less than two minutes later, he converted a three-point play with the rookie whistled for the foul, then finished a dunk after Victor Wembanyama picked off a Lendeborg pass. READ MORE: ‘Probably No Chance He’s Back in Two Weeks’ — Draymond Green Gets Blunt About Stephen Curry Injury San Antonio’s edge went well beyond Castle. The Spurs led by as many as 43, shot 48% from the field to Golden State’s 33%, and outscored the Warriors 56-28 in the paint. Lendeborg’s next test comes Monday, when the Warriors visit the New Orleans Pelicans. With Curry set to be re-evaluated in two weeks, the bigger role the rookie spoke about Friday morning remains his for now. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.description: Frenkie de Jong explains why he asked to be substituted against Greece: ‘I’ve just come back from an injury’ Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong has explained why he requested to be substituted at half-time during the Netherlands’ 7-0 victory over Greece, revealing that the decision was just precautionary after his recent return from injury. The 29-year-old captained the Netherlands in the Nations League encounter but did not feature after the interval. His withdrawal initially raised concerns about his fitness, particularly after Netherlands head coach Xavi Hernandez revealed that the midfielder had experienced back discomfort before the match. However, De Jong has now offered further context, explaining that his limited match fitness, recent injury history and demanding international schedule made continuing unnecessary with the Netherlands already leading comfortably. De Jong explains why he asked to come off against Greece Speaking after the Netherlands’ emphatic victory, De Jong was asked whether his substitution was precautionary or whether he had experienced a physical problem. “Well, it was 5-0 at half-time. Frenkie de Jong was taken off at half-time. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) “And with all this travelling and international fixtures, and my history of injuries as well, of course, there was no need to take any risks,” he explained. The midfielder’s explanation clearly shows that the comfortable scoreline played an important role in the decision. Rather than pushing himself through another 45 minutes, he preferred to avoid unnecessary physical demands while returning to full fitness. De Jong outlines Xavi’s philosophy and long-term ambitions Apart from his fitness, De Jong also discussed the Netherlands’ impressive performance and the playing philosophy Xavi wants to establish. He credited the team’s positioning and clinical finishing for the result. “I think today, quite simply, we got it right in terms of how we positioned ourselves. “And, of course, we also finished off the chances we created, the first one straight away. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) De Jong also explained the principles behind Xavi’s approach, stating, “Yes, it depends, of course, on the match each time. It’s not as if we’ve got there yet just because we’ve played one good match. item.title: UCLA HC Bob Chesney leads Bruins to best start of the 21st century with win over Illinois
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images UCLA HC Bob Chesney leads Bruins to best start of the 21st century with win over Illinois appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A soggy Friday night and a frightening quarterback injury could not slow down the No. 4 UCLA Bruins. Head coach Bob Chesney guided his squad to a gritty 22-14 victory over the Illinois Fighting Illini on Nov. 13 at the Rose Bowl, pushing UCLA to 10-0 for the first time in the 21st century. The Bruins matched the single-season school record for wins and joined Bob Toledo’s 1998 group and the 1946 squad as the only teams in program history to open a campaign with 10 straight victories. UCLA struck fast on its opening drive when quarterback Ty Dieffenbach hit wide receiver Aidan Mizell for a 54-yard touchdown. Mizell dominated the wet conditions with six catches for 176 yards, accounting for nearly half of UCLA’s 361 total yards. Disaster nearly derailed the celebration late in the second quarter. Dieffenbach suffered a shoulder injury under heavy pressure with 35 seconds left in the half, forcing backup quarterback Madden Iamaleava into action. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) UCLA’s defense held the line while Dieffenbach received treatment. Defensive lineman Aiden Gobaira sacked Illinois quarterback Katin Houser in the end zone early in the third quarter for a safety, and cornerback Scooter Jackson snagged his first of two interceptions to keep the Fighting Illini off the scoreboard until late in the frame. Dieffenbach trotted back onto the field to a massive ovation and immediately delivered. He completed all five passes on a fourth-quarter march, capping it with a 26-yard touchdown strike to wide receiver Semaj Morgan, who finished with four receptions for 56 yards. Dieffenbach closed the night 13 of 20 for 232 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception. Houser threw for 176 yards and two scores, connecting with tight end Kaden Feagin and wide receiver Collin Dixon, to pull Illinois (6-4) within five points. Still, UCLA held Illinois to 240 total yards, and Jackson’s second pick with 2:42 left plus Mateen Bhaghani’s 37-yard field goal sealed the historic win.
